**Ports are committed as of 2026-08-15 (#268).** web **3100**, chat **8100**, db
**55432** — in `docker-compose.yml`, and `next dev` runs on 3100 too. Nothing
needs a `docker-compose.override.yml` any more; if one is lying around it is
redundant, and `/docker-compose.override.yml` is now gitignored (#247).
3000/8000/5432 are deliberately left free for the user's other projects.

**The one override still needed:** `LLM_PROVIDER=gcp` inline on every command
that creates or recreates the chat container —

```bash
LLM_PROVIDER=gcp make e2e-smoke KEEP_STACK=1
LLM_PROVIDER=gcp docker compose up -d --build web
```

`.env` says `LLM_PROVIDER=local` and Ollama is not installed here, so without it
the chat container fails its local-provider preflight and exits. Compose reads
shell env ahead of `.env`, so the inline prefix is enough; never edit `.env` for
this. It is easy to forget on a *rebuild* — the initial `make e2e-smoke` gets it
and a later `docker compose up -d web` silently does not.

**A failure that looks like a code bug and is not (#270).** In a long-running
container the image optimiser can wedge: specific `(image, width)` variants stop
responding entirely — 40s with no reply — while other variants of the same image
serve in milliseconds, with nothing in `docker compose logs web`. It cost a long
misdiagnosis. Symptom: `image-delivery.spec.ts › the category grid image is
sized to its box` blows its 240s budget where it normally takes ~58s.
`docker compose restart web` clears it. Suspect this before suspecting the diff.

**Do not clear `.next/cache/images` inside a running container** — it appears to
leave the optimiser holding state for entries that no longer exist, and it
contaminated the evidence above.

**Never run two Playwright suites against one stack.** They contend and produce
timeouts that read exactly like the contention bugs being investigated.

**Why this matters:** every item here produces a failure that looks like the
change under test. The provider one exits a container, the wedge times out a
spec, the concurrency one fails scattered journeys.

**How to apply:** stand the stack up with the inline provider, verify identity
before trusting any run (`curl -s http://localhost:3100/products/category/tents |
grep -c Tents` — port 3100 has been raced by another project once), and restart
the web container before concluding a spec regression is real.

Session update, continuing the two entries above. `main` at 5d31b0e, clean. #295, #294 and #306 closed. Six issues filed and three extended.

## What landed

- **#295** — `ruff` 0.16.2 -> 0.16.3, `uvicorn` 0.52.1 -> 0.52.3.
- **#294** — `google-cloud-aiplatform` 1.163.0 -> 1.164.0.
- **#306** — the navigation drawer was not a dialog. It is now.

## The standard that made the dependency bumps quick

Both dependabot PRs were verified by showing the change **cannot reach this code**, not by observing that the checks passed. That turned out to be faster than the alternative and much more conclusive:

- `ruff`'s 0.16.3 rule changes are all in `pylint`, `flake8-bandit`, `numpy` and a preview `pyupgrade` rule; `.ruff.toml` selects `["E", "F", "I"]`, and ruff's own resolved settings dump confirms `preview = disabled` and no per-file ignores. It also never enters the chat image — the Dockerfile installs `requirements-core.txt` only.
- `uvicorn` 0.52.2/0.52.3 only touch the bundled `zttp` backend. Reading `protocols/http/auto.py` in the installed package settles it: a two-branch httptools/h11 resolver with **no reference to `zttp` at all**, so it is unreachable without an explicit `--http zttp` that no invocation site passes. That is a property of the release, so it holds inside the container too.
- `aiplatform`: the 1.163.0 wheel downloaded and diffed against 1.164.0. The modules this repo imports are byte-identical. Three *reachable* modules did change — `_generative_models.py` imports `aiplatform_v1beta1.types` — and all three changes are additive protobuf fields on unused field numbers.

**"The modules we import are unchanged" does not mean "nothing reachable changed."** `code-review` caught that on the aiplatform bump: my summary was scoped to `vertexai/` and the reachable changes were under `google/cloud/`. The conclusion survived on better evidence; the reasoning as first written did not.

Also worth carrying: `verifier` refused to accept CI as green because the run had graded the **pre-rebase** head. The operational form of step 10's rule is narrower than the rule — **check the check's `head_sha`, not the PR's colour** — and it is one `gh api` call.

## #306 is where the lesson is

The drawer is now `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal`, focus moved in, Tab trapped, Escape scoped to its own subtree, the page held still, the backdrop out of the tab order, and focus returned to the trigger. Eleven mutations, each demonstrated red.

**And after ten of those rows were green, and two rendered passes had walked the tab order in a real browser at three viewports, Shift+Tab from the panel still left the dialog** — landing on the header's Sign Up link underneath the backdrop, which is the exact defect #306 was filed for. The panel is the focus target on open and its own `tabindex="-1"` excludes it from the focusable list, so it was neither `first` nor `last` and no branch fired.

Every check began by tabbing forward, and forward from the panel happens to work.

This issue already records "an assertion can be satisfied by the thing going wrong" from #175. This is its neighbour and it deserves its own name: **a hole sits under a complete table when every entry in it starts from the same state.** The table was not wrong and the rendered passes were not wrong; they shared a starting position, and the defect lived in the one state none of them started from. Worth asking of any guard suite: *what state does every one of these begin in, and what is reachable that none of them begin in?*

The fix was then confirmed from eight entry states at two viewports, plus 25 Shift+Tabs with a capturing `focusin` listener recording zero escapes.

## Prose that asserted what nothing verified, four times, all mine

The recurring one, in a new concentration — four in a single change:

1. Focus return "by any route": the link-follow route ends on `<body>`, because Next's route-change reset runs after the effect.
2. Setting `body`'s overflow "moves nothing" here. **False** — overflow propagates from the body to the viewport when the root's is `visible`, and `chat.tsx:124` locks this same page through `body` correctly. That comment would have sent the next reader to fix working code.
3. Corrected (2) to say `documentElement` avoids a live save/restore collision with chat. **Also false** — nothing can hold both locks today: chat's `inert` covers the header below `lg`, the `z-50` backdrop covers the launcher, and chat's focus-out closes it above.
4. "leaves the viewport by about scrollY=60", contradicting its own next clause. It is 43 exactly. Four of five numbers in that comment checked out to the pixel; that one did not.

(3) is the one to remember: **the replacement for a wrong reason is a new claim, and it needs checking as hard as the original.** I only caught it by asking for it to be attacked specifically, having just been caught on (2) in the same paragraph.

## Three defects introduced by fixes to other defects

Each rendered round found something the previous round's fix had created:

- `tabIndex={-1}` plus programmatic focus makes Chromium match `:focus-visible`, drawing the UA ring around the whole 320px panel.
- Closing from a scrolled position jumped the page to the top, on all three close routes. **My own check of this read clean because it ran at `scrollY=0`, where the jump is a no-op.** The sample I chose was the one where the bug cannot appear — the "three sampled viewports" lesson on a different axis.
- The Shift+Tab hole above, introduced by the focus-into-panel behaviour that fixed the original defect.

## Method notes worth keeping

- **A rendered review must be handed a build of the change.** A `make` invocation failed because the shell's cwd had persisted into `apps/web`, and a `next start` still answered 200 — serving the *previous* build. Handing that over would have produced a confident review of pre-change code. Now verified by grepping the served bundle for a string only the new code contains, before every handover.
- `ui-review` corrected itself twice: `element.focus()` from `page.evaluate` does not satisfy Chromium's `:focus-visible` heuristic, so its first focus-ring pass reported no rings anywhere; and `page.click()` performs an actionability scroll, so its first scroll measurement was measuring Playwright rather than the app. Both were caught before reporting.
- **`document.scrollingElement` is `undefined` under jsdom.** The first scroll lock guarded on it and silently did nothing. The unit test caught it immediately; reading the code would not have.

## Housekeeping

- I was editing directly on `main` for #306 and caught it only at commit time. Step 2 says branch first; nothing enforces it, and the whole change was written before I noticed.
- Ports 3201/3202, the baseline worktree, and all review servers are gone. The `petspotr-*` containers on this machine belong to another project and were left alone.

## New issues

- **#315** — the drawer's controls draw the UA default focus ring while page controls use `ACTION_FOCUS`, and neither enforcing spec lists them. Same shape as #154: a guard that reads a list, and a surface not on it.
- **#316** — at phone width an open chat panel makes the drawer unreachable, because chat inerts `<main>` and `Header` renders inside it. Two modal surfaces, only one of which suppresses the other.
- **#317** — the drawer trigger has no focus indicator at all, which #306 turns into a focus *destination*. The mechanism works and the feedback does not.
- **#318** — every page load fetches `/api/categories` for a drawer most visitors never open.
- **#311** — `evaluate.py:110` passes `to_markdown`'s `mode` positionally; breaks on pandas 4.0.
- **#312** — `google-cloud-storage` is an unpinned transitive dependency aiplatform has announced it will drop.
- **#313** — **`vertexai.generative_models` is past its announced removal date** (June 24 2026; today is later than that) and five chat files import it, including the live GCP chat path. Nothing in this repo makes a real credentialed `generate_content` call at any version, so a green run proves the import surface resolves and nothing more.
- **#314** — `seed_gcp_all.py` reinstalls on every run and pip-installs the deliberately-excluded `vertexai` outside the constraints policy.

Extended rather than duplicated: **#219** (the duplicate `<main>` is the layout plus three pages, not just `/contact`), **#307** (`/contact` has no `Header` either — which reframes it as a missing layout rather than an auth-page oversight), **#308** (`useState([])` infers `never[]`, so the failure branch it asks for could not be typed).

## Next

**#313** is the one with a clock on it, and it is the only open item where the cost of waiting rises on its own. Nothing else is urgent.

By value after that: **#286** remains the only open user-facing functional defect and still needs its page sweep. **#317** is small, and #306 just made it matter. **#296** and **#297** are cheap and both land on `detect_changed_surfaces.py`. **#309** would stop the class of drift #260 came from.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

echo "Starting Chat Service Entrypoint..."

provider="${LLM_PROVIDER:-gcp}"
if [[ "${provider}" == "local" ]]; then
    echo "Running local-provider preflight..."

    if ! python3 local_provider_health.py; then
        echo "Local-provider preflight failed. Start Ollama and ensure the model exists:" >&2
        echo "  ollama serve" >&2
        echo "  ollama pull \${LOCAL_MODEL_NAME:-gemma3:12b}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    echo "Running local product indexing for vector search..."
    # Retry in case DB is still starting up.
    for i in {1..5}; do
        if python3 infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py; then
            break
        fi
        echo "Indexing attempt ${i} failed; retrying in 5s..."
        sleep 5

import os
import asyncio
from prisma import Prisma
import chromadb
from chromadb.utils import embedding_functions

# Path to ChromaDB persistence directory
CHROMA_DB_PATH = os.getenv("CHROMA_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '../data/chroma_db'))

async def index_products():
    print("Starting local product indexing...")
    
    try:
        # 1. Fetch products from DB
        db = Prisma()
        await db.connect()
        products = await db.product.find_many(include={'category': True, 'brand': True})
        await db.disconnect()
        
        if not products:
            print("No products found in database. Skipping indexing.")
            return

        print(f"Fetched {len(products)} products from database.")

        # 2. Initialize ChromaDB
        os.makedirs(CHROMA_DB_PATH, exist_ok=True)
        
        client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)
        ef = embedding_functions.DefaultEmbeddingFunction()
        
        # get_or_create_collection is idempotent
        collection = client.get_or_create_collection(name="products", embedding_function=ef)

        # 3. Prepare data
        documents = []
        metadatas = []
        ids = []

        for p in products:
            category_name = p.category.name if p.category else "Unknown"
            brand_name = p.brand.name if p.brand else "Unknown"
            
            doc_text = f"Product: {p.name}\nCategory: {category_name}\nBrand: {brand_name}\nDescription: {p.description or ''}\nPrice: ${p.price}"
            documents.append(doc_text)
            
            metadatas.append({
                "id": p.id,
                "name": p.name,
                "price": p.price,
                "slug": p.slug,
                "category": category_name,
                "brand": brand_name
            })
            
            ids.append(p.id)

        # 4. Add to ChromaDB
        if ids:
            # upsert is idempotent (updates if ID exists, otherwise inserts)
            collection.upsert(
                documents=documents,
                metadatas=metadatas,
                ids=ids
            )
            print(f"Successfully indexed {len(ids)} products to {CHROMA_DB_PATH}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error during indexing: {e}")
        # Don't exit with error to avoid breaking the master seed script
        # but print the traceback for debugging if needed
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(index_products())

Enough to decide. Here's what I found and the plan.

**Queue state:** The handover comment (#148, newest) ranks `#313 → #286 → #317 → #296/#297 → #309`. Since that comment a later session landed #317, #219, #311, #314, #321, #324 without appending a handover — so the live queue is narrower than the comment suggests.

**Two things worth flagging before I start:**

1. **#327 duplicates #286.** Identical measurements (`Send Message` 48–342 × 796–848; launcher 334–374 × 788–828; 8×32 px intersection). #327 was filed during the #219 review without noticing #286 already existed.
2. **#323's stale rationale is provable.** `index_products_local.py` swallows exceptions with the comment *"Don't exit with error to avoid breaking the master seed script"* — but the only remaining caller is the entrypoint retry loop (`services/chat/src/api/chat-entrypoint.sh:20`); #321/#325 removed it from the GCP seeding path. So the reason the bug exists no longer applies.

**Plan — two independent tracks:**

| Track | Issue | Surface | Needs stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **#286** chat launcher overlaps `/contact` submit at phone width | `apps/web` | yes (rendered review + journeys) |
| B | **#323** indexing failures exit zero, defeating entrypoint retries | `services/chat`, `infrastructure/scripts` | no |

They share no files and no merge gate. I'll run B's implementation while the web images build in the background for A. Follow-on: #297 + #296 (both `detect_changed_surfaces.py`, cheap, tooling-only).

I'm skipping **#313** as the lead despite its clock: it's a five-file SDK migration whose own issue says the replacement's coverage is *"not established"* and that no test in the repo makes a real `generate_content` call — that's a scoped investigation, not a thin slice, and the removal is 2 months overdue with no sign of landing.

gh issue create --title "An unseeded database is indistinguishable from a successful index, so startup never retries it" --body 'Found while fixing #323, which makes `index_products_local.py` exit nonzero when indexing *raises*. This is the neighbouring case that #323 does not cover, and it was left out of that branch deliberately rather than folded in, because whether it should be a failure is a judgement call rather than a bug fix.

## Measured

`infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py` returns early when the query comes back empty:

```python
if not products:
    print("No products found in database. Skipping indexing.")
    return
```

Run through the real script with a stubbed Prisma returning `[]`, after the #323 fix is in place:

```
empty-database run -> returncode 0
stdout: Starting local product indexing...
        No products found in database. Skipping indexing.
upserted: None
```

Exit 0. So `chat-entrypoint.sh` breaks out of its retry loop on the first attempt and the chat service starts serving with an empty vector collection.

## Why this is the same shape as #323, one step over

The retry loop exists for a startup race — its own comment says `# Retry in case DB is still starting up`. But "the database is still starting up" and "the database is up and has not been seeded yet" are the same race seen from two points, and only the first one currently retries. Compose brings `db`, seeding, and `chat` up together, so an empty read during startup is exactly the window the loop was written for.

The result is quieter than a crash: chat comes up healthy, answers questions, and grounds them in nothing. There is no error anywhere, because from the indexer`s point of view nothing went wrong.

## Why it is not obviously a bug

An empty catalogue is legitimately empty in some setups, and retrying five times with a 5s sleep before starting would cost 25s of startup on every one of them. So the options differ in policy, not just code:

1. Treat empty as a failure and let the existing loop retry it. Correct for the race, costs 25s on a genuinely empty catalogue.
2. Treat empty as a failure only when a seed is expected — e.g. gated on an env var the compose seeding path sets.
3. Leave it, and make the log line say plainly that the service is starting with no index, so the silence is at least audible.

## Not established

- Whether the compose startup ordering already makes the empty window unreachable in practice. `depends_on` conditions and the seeding step`s placement decide that, and I did not measure it — #323`s scope was the exception path, and the guard added there (`tests/scripts/test_local_indexing_retry.py`) stubs the database rather than composing a real one.
- How long the seeding step actually takes against a cold volume, which is what sets the size of the window.

The guard file above already has an `empty` failure mode wired into its Prisma stub, so whichever option is chosen has a place to be tested from.' 2>&1 | tail -2

gh issue create --title "e2e-smoke-full installs the local stack but never selects it, so \"full local-provider confidence\" is not what it buys" --body 'Found while verifying #323, whose fix lands in a code path only `LLM_PROVIDER=local` reaches. Establishing what green means for that change turned up a gap in the target that is supposed to cover it.

## The claim

Root `AGENTS.md`, in the validation matrix:

> - Full local-provider integration confidence: `make e2e-smoke-full`

## Measured

`e2e-smoke-full` sets one variable, and it is a Docker **build arg**, not a runtime provider selection:

```make
e2e-smoke-full: ## Run dockerized smoke with full chat dependency profile
	$(MAKE) e2e-smoke CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK=1
```

`CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK` has exactly one consumer:

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml:78
INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK: ${CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK:-0}
```

The provider is resolved separately and defaults to `gcp`:

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml:93
- LLM_PROVIDER=${LLM_PROVIDER:-gcp}
```

And `chat-entrypoint.sh` branches on that value, not on which dependencies are installed:

```bash
provider="${LLM_PROVIDER:-gcp}"
if [[ "${provider}" == "local" ]]; then
    # preflight, then the indexing retry loop
else
    echo "Skipping local product indexing: LLM_PROVIDER=${provider}."
fi
```

So `e2e-smoke-full` installs `chromadb`, the embedding stack and the rest of the local profile into the image, and then runs a container that takes the `gcp` branch and never uses any of it. The difference between `e2e-smoke` and `e2e-smoke-full` is image size and build time, not code coverage.

Confirmed on a real run this session (`LLM_PROVIDER=gcp make e2e-smoke KEEP_STACK=1`, which is the plain profile but exercises the same branch):

```
$ docker compose logs chat | grep -i indexing
chat-1  | Starting Chat Service Entrypoint...
chat-1  | Skipping local product indexing: LLM_PROVIDER=gcp.
```

No CI workflow sets `LLM_PROVIDER` at all — `grep -rn "LLM_PROVIDER" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns nothing — and `ci.yml:292` pins `CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK=0`. So on CI the local provider branch has never run.

## Why it matters beyond the naming

The local branch is not a thin wrapper. Behind that `if` sit the local-provider preflight, the product indexing step, and the retry loop that #323 was filed against. All of it is unexecuted by every automated target in the repository, while the matrix names a target that reads as covering it.

This is the same shape as the coverage bound recorded in #313 for the GCP path — a green run proving an import surface resolves and nothing about behaviour — except here the documentation actively asserts the coverage exists.

## Why it is not simply "add LLM_PROVIDER=local"

Selecting the local provider makes the preflight a hard prerequisite: `chat-entrypoint.sh` exits 1 if `local_provider_health.py` fails, and that needs a reachable Ollama with the model pulled. On a CI runner that means either a service container running Ollama and a model pull (`gemma3:12b` is not small), or a stub. So the fix is a decision about how much the local path is worth, not a one-line edit.

Options, roughly in increasing cost:

1. **Correct the documentation** to say what the target does — a dependency-profile build check — and drop the "local-provider integration confidence" claim. Cheapest, and stops the matrix overstating its coverage.
2. **Make `e2e-smoke-full` set `LLM_PROVIDER=local`** and gate it on a reachable Ollama, skipping loudly rather than silently taking the gcp branch when there is none.
3. **Stand up a stub provider** good enough to satisfy the preflight, so the indexing and retry path runs in CI.

## Not established

- Whether the local profile'"'"'s extra dependencies are exercised anywhere else, which decides whether option 1 leaves the target with any purpose at all.
- What the preflight actually requires of Ollama beyond reachability and model presence — I did not read `local_provider_health.py` closely, since the scope here was establishing what the target selects, not what it would take to satisfy it.' 2>&1 | tail -2

Issue #323. `services/chat/src/api/chat-entrypoint.sh` retries `infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py` *while it exits nonzero*:

```bash
for i in {1..5}; do

```

The indexer caught every indexing exception, logged it, and returned normally — so a failed index exited 0, the loop broke on attempt 1, and the retry policy was dead code. The fix re-raises after logging and exits 1 from `__main__`.

- `infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py` (modified)
- `tests/scripts/test_local_indexing_retry.py` (new, untracked — root guard suite)

`chat-entrypoint.sh` is deliberately NOT modified; the loop was already correct.

**The removed comment.** The old code carried `# Don't exit with error to avoid breaking the master seed script`. I checked that rationale before removing it: the only remaining caller of this script is the entrypoint retry loop (`grep -rn index_products_local` returns just `services/chat/Dockerfile:58` which COPYs it, and `chat-entrypoint.sh:20` which runs it). #321/#325 removed it from the GCP seeding path. Please sanity-check that reasoning independently — if there is still a caller that depends on exit 0, this change is wrong.

**Red phase.** Two assertions failed before the fix with `0 == 0` on the exit status, with tracebacks showing the real script reaching the stubs at lines 16 and 61.

- drop the logging, keep the exit status -> `test_failure_is_still_reported` failed
- loop breaks unconditionally -> `test_a_failing_attempt_is_retried_until_it_succeeds` failed `1 != 3`
- retry budget 5 -> 3 -> `test_a_permanently_failing_indexer_gives_up_and_still_serves` failed `3 != 5`
- success never breaks the loop -> `test_retrying_stops_at_the_first_success` failed `5 != 1`

Both mutated files were restored from backups and the suite is green.

**Verifier result (step 7, passed, no blockers):** `make test-scripts`, `make -C services/chat ci`, `make -C apps/web ci`, `make toolchain-doctor`, `make env-contract-check` all pass. It also rebuilt the chat image and ran the changed code *from the bytes inside the image* against stubs, getting exit code 1. And it confirmed `make e2e-smoke` never reaches this code because the entrypoint takes the `gcp` branch.

**Known bounds, already filed as issues rather than fixed here** — please do not re-report these as defects in this diff, but do tell me if you think any of them actually blocks this change:
- #332 — an empty (unseeded) database also exits 0 and is not retried. Left out because whether "empty" is a failure is a policy call.
- #333 — `make e2e-smoke-full`, documented as "full local-provider integration confidence", only sets a Docker build arg and still runs `LLM_PROVIDER=gcp`, so no automated target in the repo executes the local indexing branch at all.
- No test asserts the Dockerfile COPY actually lands this file in the image (the verifier checked it by hand this session).

## What I most want checked

1. The test file is the substantial part of the diff. Is the stubbing honest — does it exercise the real script and the real entrypoint, or has it quietly become a test of its own stubs? `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md` has specific fixture-isolation and vacuity rules; please apply them.
2. The fake `python3`/`uvicorn`/`sleep` on `PATH` for the entrypoint test — is `sleep` being stubbed away legitimate here, or does it hide something the loop depends on?
3. Whether re-raising from `index_products()` changes anything for a caller that imports the function rather than running the script.
4. Style/consistency with the surrounding Python. Note that per #330, `infrastructure/scripts/` is currently outside the enforced Ruff scope, so lint will not have caught anything here.

content.text: Now I have the real picture, and it **contradicts #286's proposed fix**. Let me record the measurement before deciding.

input.command:
cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso
gh issue comment 286 --body 'Ran the sweep this issue asks for, against a real stack at `127.0.0.1:3100`, sampling **five scroll positions per route** (0, 25%, 50%, 75%, end) across four viewports. Interactive controls were collected with `a[href], button, input, select, textarea`, intersected against the launcher rect, and every intersecting control was probed with `document.elementFromPoint` on a 50x5 grid to see where the launcher actually wins the hit test.

## First, a correction to my own method, because it changes the conclusion

My first pass scrolled each route to the document end before measuring and reported **every route clear, including `/contact`**. That is wrong, and it is wrong in an instructive way: the launcher is `fixed`, so scrolling moves the button up and out from under it. `/contact` at 390x844 has a `scrollMax` of only 116px, and by the end of that scroll the button has cleared the launcher entirely.

So the defect lives in the *landing and partial-scroll* states, and the one sample I took was the single position where it cannot appear. #148 already records this trap from the other direction ("my own check read clean because it ran at `scrollY=0`, where the jump is a no-op"). Same hole, mirrored. Re-measured across the scroll range below.

## `/contact` reproduces exactly

At 390x844, `scrollY=0` — matching this issue and #327 to the pixel:

```
Send Message  rect=[48,796,342,848]  overlap=8x32  launcherWinsHitTest=2/245  belowFold=true
launcher      rect=[334,788,374,828]
```

It persists through the scroll range and only clears at the end:

```
scrollY=0    overlap=8x32   hitTest=2/245   belowFold=true
scrollY=29   overlap=8x31   hitTest=2/245   belowFold=false
scrollY=58   overlap=8x2    hitTest=0/245   belowFold=false
scrollY=116  (end)  clear
```

**A second control on the same page, not previously reported.** At 360x740 the message `textarea` is hit as well, and worse than the button:

```
scrollY=0   TEXTAREA  rect=[48,680,312,800]  overlap=8x40  hitTest=1/147  belowFold=true
scrollY=62  TEXTAREA  rect=[48,618,312,738]  overlap=8x40  hitTest=1/245  belowFold=false
```

At 414x896 the overlap shrinks to 8x8 and the launcher wins no sampled point, so the severity is viewport-dependent.

## What the sweep rules out

**Option 1 as written does not work.** "Bottom padding on `main` at phone widths" cannot fix this. The overlap is at `scrollY=0` on a page whose content already overflows the viewport, and `padding-bottom` does not move content at `scrollY=0` — it only makes the document taller. I checked the arithmetic against the rendered numbers: content starts at y=48 and the button sits at 796 regardless of what padding follows it. Adding padding would increase `scrollMax` and leave the landing state byte-identical.

There is a structural reason too: `layout.tsx` puts the copyright `Block` *inside* `<main>`, so bottom padding on `main` lands below the footer and shows page background under the dark bar on every route.

**Horizontal separation is the only thing that holds.** The button is full-width and the launcher is fixed, so for any vertical position the button passes through the launcher band as the page scrolls. The only geometry that guarantees no intersection is the control stopping short of the launcher column: at 390 the launcher owns x >= 334, and the form card runs 48..342 with symmetric 48px margins — it overlaps by 8px because the card is 8px too wide, not because it sits at the wrong height.

## The bigger finding: `/contact` is not the worst case

The catalogue and home routes overlap the launcher at **every** viewport including tablet, at every scroll position, by the launcher`s full 40x40:

```
/products/category/tents  390x844   every product card link   overlap=40x40, hitTest up to 5/245
/products/category/tents  834x1112  every product card link   overlap=40x40
/                         414x896   "Alpine Explorer Tent"    overlap=40x24, hitTest 5/49
/                         834x1112  "TrekStar Hiking Sandals" overlap=40x40, hitTest 3/245
```

That is a much larger surface than `/contact`, and it is *not* obviously a defect: `chat-launcher.spec.ts` states in its own header that "covering content is tolerable", and #187 already tracks the panel covering product links. So the catalogue overlap is a standing decision rather than an oversight, and reopening it is a policy call.

Filing that separately rather than folding it in. What makes `/contact` different, and worth fixing on its own, is that the covered control is the page`s single primary action, the mis-tap opens a modal over a part-composed form, and `chat.tsx` already applies exactly that reasoning one control over — its close-button comment calls a mis-tap that "discards the message being composed" a defect worth moving a control for.

## Open decision

Given option 1 is ruled out, the fix is a reserved launcher column at phone widths. Whether that is scoped to the contact form or expressed as a shared constant other pages can opt into is the remaining call, and I am asking before implementing rather than picking one.' 2>&1 | tail -2

Interactive controls collected with `a[href], button, input, select, textarea`, intersected against the launcher rect, then probed with `document.elementFromPoint` on a 50x5 grid per control to find where the launcher actually wins the hit test. Five scroll positions per route (0, 25%, 50%, 75%, end).

```
route                     viewport    control                          overlap  launcherWinsHitTest
/products/category/tents  390x844     TrailMaster X4 Tent $250.00      40x40    0/196
/products/category/tents  390x844     TrailBlazer Trailhead $490.00    40x40    5/245
/products/category/tents  360x740     TrailMaster X4 Tent $250.00      40x40    6/147
/products/category/tents  360x740     PeakPerformance Backpacker $330  40x40    6/245
/products/category/tents  834x1112    NatureNest Shelter $465.00       40x40    0/147
/                         414x896     Alpine Explorer Tent             40x24    5/49
/                         834x1112    TrekStar Hiking Sandals          40x40    3/245
/                         834x1112    CompactCook Camping Stove        40x39    5/49
```

The pattern is the same at every scroll position sampled: the grid is full-bleed (cards run x=12..378 at 390 wide), the launcher is `fixed bottom-0 right-0` with `mr-4 mb-4`, so whichever card happens to be in the bottom-right corner is covered. Scrolling does not help — it just changes which card it is.

`/about`, `/login` and `/signup` are clear at every viewport and scroll position tested.

## Why this is filed as a question, not a bug

There is an explicit written decision that this is acceptable. `apps/web/e2e/chat-launcher.spec.ts`, in its header:

> A floating launcher covers page content — it is fixed and the content scrolls under it, so a bottom gutter would only help at the very end of a document — and covering content is tolerable. Covering it with something the eye reads as part of the page is not

So the overlap itself was considered and accepted; what #190 fixed was the launcher being *invisible* against what it covered, not that it covered things. #187 tracks the related case for the chat panel at 1024+.

What the measurement adds is the scale — this is not an edge case, it is every catalogue page at every viewport — and the hit-test numbers, which show the launcher genuinely winning taps on product links rather than merely overlapping them visually.

## What is actually at stake

A product card is a large target (~446px tall at phone) and the launcher covers 40x40 of its corner, so the mis-tap rate is low and the cost of a mis-tap is small: the chat opens, the user closes it, nothing is lost. That is a real difference from #286, where the covered control is a form`s primary action and a mis-tap opens a modal over a part-composed message.

So the honest framing is: this is tolerable by the standard already written down, and the reason to revisit it would be a decision that the launcher should never win a tap on page content, not that any individual card is broken.

## Options

1. **Leave it, and say so where the sweep will find it next time.** Record the measurement in `chat-launcher.spec.ts``s header next to the existing claim, so the next person to run this sweep does not re-derive it as a defect. Cheapest, and keeps the existing decision intact.
2. **Reserve the launcher column in the grid** at the affected viewports, so the last card in a row stops short of it. Costs layout symmetry on every catalogue page to fix a low-cost mis-tap.
3. **Make the launcher yield** — shrink or translate it when a interactive element is under it. Most invasive, and the launcher moving under the pointer is its own usability problem.

Option 1 is what the existing written decision implies. Recording the numbers is the part that is missing.

## Not established

- Whether the hit-test misses (`0/245` on several rows) mean those cards are genuinely unaffected or only that the sample grid stepped over the 40x40 corner. The grid is 2% of the control width horizontally and 5 rows vertically, so on a 446px-tall card the vertical steps are ~89px and can straddle a 40px band. The `40x40` geometric overlap is exact; the hit-test count is a lower bound, not a measurement of severity.
- Whether keyboard focus ever lands on a covered card in a state where the launcher is on top — `chat-modality.spec.ts` guards that for the panel, not for the launcher.' 2>&1 | tail -2

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso
gh issue create --title "The indexing retry loop sleeps and announces a retry after its final attempt" --body 'Found by `code-review` during #323. The lines are not touched by that change, but #323 is what makes them reachable: until the indexer reported failure as a nonzero exit, the loop always broke on attempt 1 and the fifth-attempt path had never run.

## Measured

`services/chat/src/api/chat-entrypoint.sh`:

```bash
for i in {1..5}; do
    if python3 infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py; then
        break
    fi
    echo "Indexing attempt ${i} failed; retrying in 5s..."
    sleep 5
done
```

The `echo` and the `sleep` sit after the `if`, inside the loop body, with nothing distinguishing the last iteration. So when attempt 5 fails, the shell prints `Indexing attempt 5 failed; retrying in 5s...`, sleeps 5 seconds, and then falls out of the loop to `exec uvicorn`.

Two costs, both small and both real:

- **5 seconds of startup latency** that buys nothing, on the path where the service is already degraded.
- **A log line that is false.** It says a retry is coming when the loop is finished. An operator reading container logs during an incident sees "retrying" as the last indexing message and reasonably concludes the retry is still in flight.

## Reproduced

`tests/scripts/test_local_indexing_retry.py::test_a_permanently_failing_indexer_gives_up_and_still_serves` drives exactly this path with a stub indexer that always fails. It asserts 5 attempts and that `uvicorn` still starts, so it pins the retry budget and the give-up behaviour — but it stubs `sleep` away and does not assert on the log text, so it passes either way.

## Suggested fix

Guard both on not being the last iteration, e.g.

```bash
if [ "${i}" -lt 5 ]; then
    echo "Indexing attempt ${i} failed; retrying in 5s..."
    sleep 5
fi
```

and say something true when the budget is exhausted — the service starts without a vector index, which is worth one line of log rather than silence.

The retry count is currently a literal in two places once you count the guard test`s expected `5`. Lifting it to a variable would remove that, but that is a judgement call about shell style rather than part of this defect.

## Not established

Whether 5 attempts at 5s is the right budget at all. `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` has its own wait timeouts for the same startup window and I did not compare them, so the loop may be shorter or longer than the thing it is waiting for.' 2>&1 | tail -1
gh issue create --title "index_products_local disconnects Prisma only on the success path" --body 'Found by `code-review` during #323, in the file that change touches but not in the lines it changes.

## Measured

`infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py`:

```python
db = Prisma()
await db.connect()
products = await db.product.find_many(include={"category": True, "brand": True})
await db.disconnect()
```

All four statements are inside the function`s single `try`. If `find_many` raises, `disconnect()` never runs and the client is left connected. There is no `finally`.

## Why it is harmless today, and why it is still worth recording

The only caller is `chat-entrypoint.sh`, and after #323 a failure exits the process — which closes the connection as a side effect of the interpreter shutting down. So today the leak lasts microseconds and costs nothing.

It stops being harmless the moment this function acquires a second caller, or is invoked in a loop, or is imported rather than run as a script. #323 deliberately made `index_products()` raise rather than swallow, precisely so it composes as a library function; this is the one thing in it that does not compose.

It is also the kind of defect that is invisible in exactly the environment where it is cheapest to fix: local runs exit immediately, and a long-lived caller is where the connection count starts mattering.

## Suggested fix

```python
db = Prisma()
await db.connect()
try:
    products = await db.product.find_many(include={"category": True, "brand": True})
finally:
    await db.disconnect()
```

Note this is a narrower `try` than the existing one and should not be merged into it — the outer `try` exists to log and re-raise, and wrapping `connect()` in the same `finally` would call `disconnect()` on a client that never connected.

## Not established

Whether `prisma-client-py` tolerates `disconnect()` on a never-connected client, which decides whether the `finally` can safely start one line earlier. I did not test it.' 2>&1 | tail -1

## What was wrong

`services/chat/src/api/chat-entrypoint.sh` retries the local product indexer **while it exits nonzero**:

```bash
for i in {1..5}; do
    if python3 infrastructure/scripts/index_products_local.py; then
        break
    fi
    echo "Indexing attempt ${i} failed; retrying in 5s..."
    sleep 5
done
```

`index_products_local.py` caught every indexing exception, logged it, and returned normally. So a failed index exited 0, the loop broke on attempt 1, and the retry policy was dead code. The chat service came up serving an empty vector collection, with the logs showing an error and then a normal startup.

The loop is **not** changed here. It was already correct; it only looked broken because nothing could make it iterate.

## The removed comment

The old code carried `# Don'"'"'t exit with error to avoid breaking the master seed script`. That was true when written and is not any more — #321 and #325 removed this script from the GCP seeding path. The only remaining references are `services/chat/Dockerfile:58` (COPY) and `chat-entrypoint.sh:20` (the retry loop). `code-review` re-derived this independently rather than taking my word for it.

## Coverage

`tests/scripts/test_local_indexing_retry.py` runs the real script and the real entrypoint rather than reading them. The existing entrypoint coverage in `test_chat_profile_wiring.py` is `assertIn` over the script text, which cannot see an exit status.

- The indexer runs as a subprocess with `prisma` and `chromadb` shadowed via `PYTHONPATH`. That picks the failure point and keeps the guard runnable under the core setup profile, which does not install `chromadb`.
- The entrypoint runs under `bash` with `python3`, `uvicorn` and `sleep` shadowed on `PATH`, so the loop is driven by a chosen exit status rather than a real database.

**Red phase:** two assertions failed `0 == 0` on the exit status, with tracebacks showing the real script reaching the stubs at lines 16 and 61.

**The other seven guard behaviour that already worked, so each was demonstrated against a deliberate break:**

| Break | Assertion that caught it |
| --- | --- |
| always exit 1, even on success | `1 != 0` |
| drop the logging, keep the exit status | stub message not found |
| loop breaks unconditionally | `1 != 3` |
| retry budget 5 -> 3 | `3 != 5` |
| success never breaks the loop | `5 != 1` |
| Dockerfile COPY destination moved | `scripts/... != infrastructure/scripts/...` |
| COPY source not in the repository | `False is not true` |
| entrypoint invokes a different path | `0 != 3`, `0 != 5`, `0 != 1` |

## A deliberate scope call

`IndexerDeliveryTests` guards lines this change does not touch. The entrypoint invokes the indexer by a relative path that resolves only because the Dockerfile copies it to exactly that destination — that seam is what delivers this fix, and nothing compared the two declarations. Per AGENTS.md`s rule about treating a seam as one contract, it seemed wrong to fix the file without pinning how it arrives.

It does **not** prove the COPY landed in the built image, and says so in its own docstring.

## What green does not prove here

`verifier` established this directly rather than by inference: **no automated target in this repository executes this code path.** The entrypoint reaches it only under `LLM_PROVIDER=local`, and smoke runs the gcp branch:

chat-1  | Skipping local product indexing: LLM_PROVIDER=gcp.

What was verified against the real artifact: the chat image was rebuilt from this branch and the changed code was run **from the bytes inside the image** against stubs, exiting 1. Before the rebuild the warm image still had the old catch-and-return code, which confirms the layers were genuinely stale rather than the check being a no-op.

`make test-scripts` (206 tests, run twice, no flakes), `make -C services/chat ci`, `make -C apps/web ci`, `make toolchain-doctor`, `make env-contract-check`, and `LLM_PROVIDER=gcp make e2e-smoke` all pass. No findings were disputed.

Findings recorded rather than folded in, per AGENTS.md:

- #332 — an unseeded database also exits 0 and is not retried. Whether "empty" is a failure is a policy call.
- #333 — `e2e-smoke-full` never selects the local provider, so the documented coverage does not exist.
- #335 — the loop sleeps 5s and announces a retry after its *final* attempt. This change makes that path reachable for the first time.
- #336 — `disconnect()` is not in a `finally`, so a mid-read failure leaves the client connected.

content.text:
`code-review` found a genuine **defect**, and it was mine — the kind this repo has a written history of.

My comment's sweep table was measured on the page-column version and carried across unchanged when the reserve moved to the card wrapper. On the shipped lever the numbers are flat: `doc=960`, `submitBottom=848` at *every* inset from 16px to 56px. The 28px cliff I'd cited belongs to the rejected placement, and its cause was the **subtitle** wrapping to a third line (`subtitleH 56→84`), not the card narrowing. So the stated reason for choosing 32px didn't hold for the code being shipped.

The real bounds, re-measured: the focus ring at the bottom (24px puts it 4px under the launcher; 28px brings it exactly to the edge; 32px is the first Tailwind step with daylight) and the spec's width floor at the top (56px leaves the submit 214px against a 234px floor).

Two things that came out of fixing it:

- I wrote a *new* claim into the comment — that the vertical-space test catches the reserve moving back to the column — and my first attempt to verify it reported all seven tests passing. That was wrong: the mutation build had **failed** on an unused import, and `up -d --build` silently kept serving the previous image. Redone faithfully, both tests do fail. content.text:
The probe contradicts #297's premise in a way that matters for whoever implements it — and the two readers behave **differently**:

| Reader | space | non-ASCII | with `quotePath=false` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git status --porcelain` | **quoted** | quoted | space still quoted, non-ASCII literal |
| `git diff --name-only` | **not quoted** | quoted | both literal |

Recording that on the issue rather than letting the next person rediscover it:

input.command:
cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso
cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-contoso/32aea79c-3855-4190-9ae4-5916c6d50c99/scratchpad/c297.md <<'EOF'
Probed this against real git before implementing, and the premise needs correcting in one place: **the two readers do not quote the same inputs**, so the fix is not symmetric between them.

## Measured

Scratch repository, three tracked files — one with a space, one with a non-ASCII byte, one plain — all modified:

```
$ git status --porcelain
 M "apps/web/src/a b.tsx"
 M "apps/web/src/na\303\257ve.tsx"
 M apps/web/src/plain.tsx

$ git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain
 M "apps/web/src/a b.tsx"          <- still quoted
 M apps/web/src/naïve.tsx
 M apps/web/src/plain.tsx
```

```
$ git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTD HEAD~1...HEAD
apps/web/src/a b.tsx               <- NOT quoted
"apps/web/src/na\303\257ve.tsx"
apps/web/src/plain.tsx

$ git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTD HEAD~1...HEAD
apps/web/src/a b.tsx
apps/web/src/naïve.tsx
apps/web/src/plain.tsx
```

So:

| reader | space | non-ASCII | after `core.quotePath=false` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git status --porcelain` (worktree) | quoted | quoted | space **still quoted**, non-ASCII literal |
| `git diff --name-only` (range) | not quoted | quoted | both literal |

The issue body says "Git C-quotes any path containing a space or a non-ASCII byte" and shows both example paths quoted under `git status --porcelain`. That is right for `status` and **wrong for `diff --name-only`**, which leaves a space alone. It does not change the conclusion — both readers need fixing — but it changes what each one needs:

- `changed_files_from_range` needs `core.quotePath=false`, after which nothing in the common cases stays quoted.
- `changed_files_from_worktree` needs `core.quotePath=false` **and** the unquoting step regardless, because a space alone still produces a quoted path there.

An implementation that adds `core.quotePath=false` to both and unquotes only where it seemed necessary from the issue body would leave the worktree reader — the one that feeds `make quick-ci-changed`, i.e. the local loop this issue says is degraded most — still broken for the most common case of all, a filename with a space.

## Two more things worth knowing before implementing

**Unquoting is still needed even with `quotePath=false`.** A literal quote character survives it:

```
$ git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain -uall
?? "apps/web/src/qu\"ote.tsx"
```

so the `"..."` unwrapper has to handle `\"`, `\\`, the control-character escapes, and `\NNN` **octal** (not hex) byte escapes, decoding to bytes and then UTF-8.

**Untracked files may never appear individually.** `git status --porcelain` summarises an untracked directory to a single entry:

```
$ git status --porcelain
?? apps/
```

Every untracked file under a new directory reaches `classify` as `apps/`, which matches no pattern and sets `unknown`. That is a *separate* path from the quoting bug and it is not mentioned in this issue — it needs `-uall` to expose, and it would change what the flag reports for any change that adds a new directory. Worth deciding deliberately rather than inheriting, since flipping it on will reclassify things.

## Renames

`git status --porcelain` renders a rename as `R  old -> new`, and either side may be quoted. The current `" -> "` split runs before any unquoting, so it also has to cope with a quoted name that contains ` -> ` inside the quotes. Parsing the first quoted token to its closing quote, then looking for the separator after it, handles that; splitting the raw string does not.

## Status

Not implemented — I measured this while picking up the issue and ran out of session before writing the fix. Session update. `main` at cbcc328, clean, stack torn down with volumes. #323 and #286 closed, #327 closed as a duplicate. Six issues filed, one corrected rather than implemented.

## What landed

- **#337 / #323** — `index_products_local.py` caught every indexing exception and returned normally, so a failed index exited 0 and `chat-entrypoint.sh` broke out of its retry loop on attempt 1. The retry policy had never run. The loop was already correct and is unchanged.
- **#340 / #286** — the fixed chat launcher took taps from `/contact`'s submit button (8x32 overlap at 390x844, `elementFromPoint` returning the launcher). `/contact` now reserves the launcher's column around its card.

## The one that generalises: a table that was right when written

`#286`'s comment carried a sweep table justifying 32px of reserve. `code-review` found it false. It had been measured on the page-container placement, `ui-review` then moved the reserve to the card wrapper, and the table came along unchanged — on the new lever, document height is flat from 16px to 56px, and the 28px cliff it cited belonged to the rejected version. Its stated cause was wrong too: the extra height came from the *subtitle* rewrapping, not the card.

Nothing could have flagged it. The code still compiled, every test still passed, and the numbers were real measurements — of a thing that no longer existed. This issue already records "prose that asserted what nothing verified"; this is the harder neighbour: **prose that was verified, against a version the change then replaced.** Worth asking whenever an implementation moves: *which measurements in the comments were taken against the old one?*

## Sampling, again, and in the opposite direction from last time

My first `/contact` sweep scrolled every route to the document end before measuring and reported **every route clean**, including the one with the filed defect. The launcher is `fixed`, `/contact` scrolls 116px, and by the end of that scroll the button has cleared it. The single position I sampled was the only one where the defect cannot appear.

The previous entry records the same hole from the other side — a check that read clean because it ran at `scrollY=0`. So the lesson is not "sample the ends" but: **the state you sample is a choice, and a defect that lives in a range will hide from any single point in it.**

## A guard that measured the transition, not the ring

The focus-ring guard read `getComputedStyle` immediately after Tab. The button carries `transition-all`, so it got the transition's *initial* values — `3px/0px`, the CSS defaults of `medium` and `currentcolor` — instead of the settled `2px/2px`. That is 1px **looser**, in the direction that lets a defect through: an 11px inset produces `gap=3`, which the transient reading scores as clearing by 0 and the settled reading correctly rejects at -1.

`AGENTS.md` already warns that `outlineWidth` reports a user-agent default for an outline whose style is `none`. This is the same trap with a clock on it — the right value arrives a few hundred milliseconds after the wrong one. Settle by polling until two consecutive samples agree, rather than by a timeout or by pinning the expected value, which would make the test fail for a change to the ring instead of to the clearance.

## Sub-agent findings are claims, in both directions

- `ui-review` reported that `element.focus()` does not satisfy Chromium's `:focus-visible`. Measured, it does — `solid 2px`, identical to the Tab path, matching what this issue records about the drawer panel. It confirmed the correction next round.
- `code-review`'s finding was right but one of its numbers was not: the wrapper's content box at 640 is 592px, not 560. Conclusion unchanged.
- Both were worth checking, and both checks were cheap. The finding I complied with without checking is the one that cost most — see the table above, which I fixed on the reviewer's word and then had to re-measure anyway because my *replacement* claim was also unverified.

## Two local mechanics that produced false results

Both now in the machine notes, and both produced a confident green:

- **`docker compose up -d --build web` starts the previous image when the build fails.** It prints the failure and carries on, so the stack stays up and answers normally. With build output redirected, there is nothing to see at all. This reported all seven assertions passing against a mutation that had never been built — the build had failed on an unused import, which is exactly what a mutation that removes the only use of a symbol produces. Run `docker compose build` as its own step and read it.
- **A 200 from :3100 does not mean the new build is serving.** A `curl -sf` readiness loop gets answered by the container being replaced. Poll for a string only the new code emits. This raced me four times in one change.

## Process note

One `verifier` invocation ended its turn with "I'll wait for the notification" and no report. It had to be resumed explicitly. An unreported run is indistinguishable from no run, so it is worth checking that a sub-agent's result actually contains findings rather than an intention to produce them.

## New issues

- **#332** — an unseeded database also exits 0 from the indexer, so startup never retries it. Policy call: 5 retries at 5s costs 25s on a genuinely empty catalogue.
- **#333** — `make e2e-smoke-full`, which `AGENTS.md` calls "full local-provider integration confidence", only sets a Docker **build arg**. Compose still resolves `LLM_PROVIDER=gcp`, no CI job sets it, and the entrypoint's local branch — preflight, indexing, retry loop — has never run in CI. The documentation asserts coverage that does not exist.
- **#334** — every product card on the catalogue and home routes sits under the launcher at every viewport, tablet included. Filed rather than changed because `chat-launcher.spec.ts` records "covering content is tolerable" as a decision.
- **#335** — the retry loop sleeps 5s and logs "retrying" after its *final* attempt. #323 made that path reachable for the first time.
- **#336** — `disconnect()` is not in a `finally`.
- **#338** — the contact form discards the error it catches.
- **#339** — `/login` and `/signup` submits also sit in the launcher's column; what saves them is that the forms are short enough not to scroll. Nothing measures that gap, so one added field reintroduces #286 on a page with no guard.

## #297 corrected rather than implemented

Probed real git before writing the fix, and the issue's premise is wrong in a way that would have produced a broken one. It says both readers C-quote paths containing a space. `git diff --name-only` does **not**; only `git status --porcelain` does, and that one keeps quoting spaces even after `core.quotePath=false`. Following the body would have left the worktree reader — the one feeding `make quick-ci-changed`, which the issue itself says is the most degraded — still broken for the commonest case.

Measurements and the reproduction are in a comment on the issue.

**#297** is the cheapest real work left and is now three commands from starting — the measurements are on the issue and the premise is corrected. **#296** lands in the same file and should follow it rather than share a branch.

After that, by value: the `/contact` cluster (**#326**, **#338**, **#339**) is now three filed defects on one page and one rendered stack would cover all three. **#333** is small and stops the validation matrix overstating itself. **#313** still has the only clock, and still wants its own slice and its own testing story — nothing in the repo makes a real credentialed `generate_content` call at any version, and #333 explains why no target ever will.

`core.quotePath=false` would turn a misclassification into a **hard crash** of `make quick-ci-changed` on a non-UTF-8 filename. Git's default quoting is ASCII-safe. Implementing the unquote-only fix, and adding a test for that case:

from pathlib import Path

old = '''def changed_files_from_range(base: str, head: str) -> list[str]:'''
new = '''# git renders a path it considers unsafe as a C-quoted string: wrapped in
# double quotes, with backslash escapes and non-ASCII bytes as three-digit
# octal. `git status --porcelain` does that for any name containing a space,
# and both readers do it for non-ASCII. Taken literally, `"apps/web/a b.tsx"`
# matches no pattern and classifies as `unknown` (#297).
_C_ESCAPES = {
    "a": 0x07,
    "b": 0x08,
    "f": 0x0C,
    "n": 0x0A,
    "r": 0x0D,
    "t": 0x09,
    "v": 0x0B,
    '"': 0x22,
    "\\\\": 0x5C,
}


def unquote_git_path(path: str) -> str:
    """Undo git's C-quoting. Returns anything unquoted unchanged.

    Not `core.quotePath=false`, which is the obvious fix and is a worse one.
    That makes git emit the raw bytes, and a filename that is not valid UTF-8
    then raises `UnicodeDecodeError` out of `subprocess.run(text=True)` --
    measured, `git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain` on a name
    containing byte 0xff dies where the default emits an ASCII-safe
    `"apps/web/src/bad\\377.tsx"`. That would turn a misclassification into a
    hard failure of `make quick-ci-changed`. The flag would also not be enough
    on its own: `status --porcelain` quotes a name containing a space whether
    it is set or not.

    Decoding is via bytes rather than str because the escapes are bytes: a
    single non-ASCII character arrives as several octal escapes, and only the
    assembled sequence is decodable.
    """
    if len(path) < 2 or not path.startswith('"') or not path.endswith('"'):
        return path

    body = path[1:-1]
    out = bytearray()
    index = 0
    while index < len(body):
        char = body[index]
        if char != "\\\\":
            out.extend(char.encode("utf-8"))
            index += 1
            continue
        index += 1
        if index >= len(body):
            break
        escape = body[index]
        if escape in "01234567":
            out.append(int(body[index : index + 3], 8))
            index += 3
            continue
        out.append(_C_ESCAPES.get(escape, ord(escape)))
        index += 1
    # surrogateescape so a name that is not valid UTF-8 survives as a distinct
    # string rather than raising or collapsing into replacement characters.
    return out.decode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")


def _read_path_token(payload: str, index: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Read one porcelain path starting at `index`, quoted or not."""
    if payload[index] == '"':
        cursor = index + 1
        while cursor < len(payload):
            if payload[cursor] == "\\\\":
                cursor += 2
                continue
            if payload[cursor] == '"':
                return payload[index : cursor + 1], cursor + 1
            cursor += 1
        return payload[index:], len(payload)
    separator = payload.find(" -> ", index)
    if separator == -1:
        return payload[index:], len(payload)
    return payload[index:separator], separator


def porcelain_destination(payload: str) -> str:
    """The path a porcelain entry is about -- for a rename, where it now is.

    Splitting the raw string on " -> " is not enough once quoting is in play,
    because a quoted name can contain that sequence. Reading the first token to
    its closing quote and looking for the separator after it cannot be fooled
    that way.
    """
    if not payload:
        return payload
    token, index = _read_path_token(payload, 0)
    if payload[index:].startswith(" -> "):
        token, _ = _read_path_token(payload, index + 4)
    return unquote_git_path(token)

## Scope

Issue #297. `scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py` took git's path output literally. Git C-quotes a path it considers unsafe — wrapped in double quotes, backslash escapes, non-ASCII as three-digit octal — so `apps/web/src/a b.tsx` arrives as `"apps/web/src/a b.tsx"`, matches no pattern, and classifies as `unknown`.

Two files:
- `scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py` — adds `unquote_git_path`, `_read_path_token` and `porcelain_destination`; both readers now unquote, and the worktree reader's rename split is quote-aware.
- `tests/scripts/test_detect_changed_surfaces.py` — a new `QuotedPathTests` class, 8 tests, driving a **real temporary git repository** rather than patching `run_git`, with `detect_changed.ROOT` rebound to the fixture.

`scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py --print-targets` reports:
`toolchain-doctor env-contract-check test-scripts quick-ci-web quick-ci-chat`

## The design decision I most want checked

**The fix deliberately does NOT use `core.quotePath=false`, which is what issue #297 recommends.** I measured that flag and it is actively worse:

```
default          text=True OK     -> 'M "apps/web/src/bad\377.tsx"'
quotePath=false  text=True RAISES -> UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff
```

With the flag, git emits raw bytes and `subprocess.run(text=True)` raises, so one non-UTF-8 filename anywhere in the worktree would take down `make quick-ci-changed` entirely instead of misclassifying one path. Git's default quoting keeps the stream ASCII. The flag would also be insufficient on its own — `git status --porcelain` quotes a name containing a space whether it is set or not, while `git diff --name-only` never quotes a space at all.

Please confirm that reasoning independently, because it is the load-bearing part of the change and it contradicts the filed issue. `test_a_filename_that_is_not_utf8_does_not_crash_the_reader` is the guard that pins it.

The whole battery step 7 asks for, scoped by the matrix. Scripts/tooling is the changed surface, so `make test-scripts` at minimum. This file decides what CI runs for every change, so please also sanity-check that the tool still behaves on ordinary input — `--print-targets` on a real range, and that a normal path still classifies as it did on `main`. A regression here would silently change CI routing for everything.

- 27 tests in `tests.scripts.test_detect_changed_surfaces`, all passing.
- Red phase: 5 of the 8 new tests failed before the fix, with the quoted strings visible in the diffs.
- Mutations demonstrated: naive `" -> "` split (separator test fails), `core.quotePath=false` (non-UTF-8 test fails with the UnicodeDecodeError above), octal decoded as decimal (non-ASCII round-trip fails).

## Not addressed here, deliberately

`git status --porcelain` collapses an untracked directory to a single entry (`?? apps/`), so files under a new directory never reach `classify` individually. That needs `-uall` and would reclassify things, so it is a separate decision — I raised it in a comment on #297 rather than folding it in. Say if you think it blocks this change.

`line.strip()` removes leading and trailing whitespace from every path. That is safe for the worktree reader, because `git status --porcelain` quotes any path containing a space — including one that only begins or ends with a space — so the strip runs against the quotes rather than the name.

It is not safe here. `git diff --name-only` does **not** quote a path for containing a space (measured during #297: `apps/web/src/a b.tsx` arrives bare). So a tracked file named `" Makefile"` or `"Makefile "` reaches `matches_any` as `Makefile`.

## Why it is nearly harmless, and where it is not

For the glob patterns it does not matter — ` apps/web/x.ts` still starts with `apps/web/` once stripped, and would have anyway.

It matters for the exact-name entries, which are most of `RUNTIME_PATTERNS`:

```
docker-compose.yml
apps/web/package.json
services/chat/constraints.txt
.github/workflows/ci.yml
```

A file named `docker-compose.yml ` with a trailing space is a different file from `docker-compose.yml`, and this classifies it as the latter — the one case where the strip changes an answer rather than tidying one. It fails in the *unsafe* direction: an unrelated file gets a real surface's routing, where the rest of this module is careful to fail towards `unknown` and the full runtime suite.

#297 fixed the quoting defect and deliberately did not touch the strip, which predates it and is present at `HEAD` in the same form. Removing it needs its own thought: the strip is also what discards the trailing newline handling for the last line, so it cannot simply be deleted without checking what `splitlines()` already guarantees.

Strip only the line terminator rather than all whitespace — `splitlines()` has already removed it, so for this reader the strip may be removable outright. The guard belongs with it: a fixture file whose tracked name has a leading or trailing space, asserted to classify as `unknown` rather than as the pattern it resembles.

git commit -F - <<'MSG'
fix(tooling): unquote the paths git C-quotes before classifying

Git renders a path it considers unsafe as a C-quoted string: wrapped in
double quotes, backslash escapes, non-ASCII as three-digit octal. Both
readers took that literally, so `apps/web/src/a b.tsx` arrived as
`"apps/web/src/a b.tsx"`, matched no pattern, and classified as unknown.

Routing fails safe -- unknown forces the full runtime recommendation --
so nothing was under-gated and this has never been visible in CI. The
cost is to the flag. #253 had just narrowed unknown so it could mean "no
pattern claims this path", and every classified file sheltering under it
makes that harder to tighten again.

The fix deliberately does not use `core.quotePath=false`, which is what
#297 recommends. Measured:

  default          text=True OK     'M "apps/web/src/bad\377.tsx"'
  quotePath=false  text=True RAISES UnicodeDecodeError, byte 0xff

With the flag git emits raw bytes and subprocess.run(text=True) raises,
so one non-UTF-8 filename anywhere in the worktree would take down
`make quick-ci-changed` entirely rather than misclassify a path. The
flag is also not sufficient alone: `git status --porcelain` quotes a
name containing a space whether it is set or not, while `git diff
--name-only` never quotes a space at all. The two readers do not quote
the same inputs, which the issue assumes they do. Both the verifier and
code-review reproduced all three measurements independently.

The rename split is now quote-aware. Splitting the raw payload on " -> "
cuts a quoted name containing that sequence in half; reading the first
token to its closing quote cannot be fooled that way. Ordinary routing
is unchanged, confirmed byte-identical against main over the full
repository history.

Coverage drives a real temporary git repository with ROOT rebound to it,
rather than patching run_git -- the defect is in what git emits, so a
fixture that fakes the output cannot exercise it. Seven of the nine
tests fail against the unfixed script; the other two were written after
the fix and are demonstrated by mutation.

tests/scripts/AGENTS.md gains a section on how those demonstrations lie,
which is in this change rather than its own because this change's whole
evidence is mutation demonstrations and both failure modes bit while
producing it. A constant-flip mutation changes neither mtime nor size,
so a restore within the same second leaves the stale .pyc considered
current -- grep shows the original source while the suite fails through
the mutated table. And a sed whose pattern never matched leaves every
test green, which is indistinguishable from an assertion that catches
nothing. The verifier hit the second one independently while checking
this change, before reading the note.

Not addressed, deliberately: `git status --porcelain` collapses an
untracked directory to a single entry, so files under a new directory
never reach classify individually. Exposing them needs -uall and would
reclassify things, so it is its own decision, recorded on #297.

Filed rather than fixed: #341.

Closes #297
